Definition: properly, to push forth; (but used only figuratively) to lash, i.e. (the sea with oars) to row; by implication, to travel
BiblicalUsage: Shut means to run to and fro, to go back and forth across the earth, and it belongs to watchers. Daniel is told many shall run to and fro and knowledge shall be increased at the time of the end, Satan answers that he comes from going to and fro in the earth, Jeremiah is told to run through the streets of Jerusalem seeking one just man, and the eyes of the Lord run to and fro through the whole earth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the running to and fro is watched from above. Satan roams, the godly search, and the eyes of the Lord range the whole earth, and I hold that nothing moving escapes His sight.
